title: Related Questions
question: Related Questions Q. One of my friends tells me that doing an umrah by wearing ahram from "masjid-e-Aisha" is permissible only for women folk and not for men. His explanation was that Nabi-e-Kareem Muhammad (Pbuh) asked aisha(radiallahu anha) to do umrah from "masjid-e-aisha" as she was sick during the time of Hajj, and her brother was not asked to do the same when he accompanied her. If this was permissible for men then Nabi-e-Kareem Muhammad (Pbuh)would have also asked him to do umrah from "masjid-e-aisha". My friend also tells me that according to Imam Abu Hanifa Rahmatulla alayh, such umrah is permissible for men but is makruh. Please quote to the exact hadith in discussion and explanation as to how and why it is permissible for men and also comment on the views of my friend. answer: Prayers & Duties >> Hajj & Umrah Question ID: 8410 Country: United States of America Title: can a women in ihram apply olive oil on her hair? (2) after a women cuts her hair in haj can a cloth touch her face? (3) the first time one sees the kabba one duas get excepted is this the first blink of the eye or as long as one remains looking at the kabba? Question: can a women in ihram apply olive oil on her hair? (2) after a women cuts her hair in haj can a cloth touch her face? (3) the first time one sees the kabba one duas get excepted is this the first blink of the eye or as long as one remains looking at the kabba? Answer ID: 8410 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1505/1262=L/1429) (1) No, she can not apply. (2) After she cuts her hair, a cloth can touch her face. (3) It is mentioned in Hadith that while seeing at Kabah the dua is accepted. This is not related to only the first look, rather one can keep on praying as long as he or she holds his look at the Kabah, the duas shall be granted in-shaAllah. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
